title: Conviction of Sin
definition: Conviction of Sin is the Holy Spirit's work of exposing sin and bringing people to see their need for repentance, forgiveness, and Christ.
summary: Conviction of Sin is the Holy Spirit's work of exposing sin and bringing people to see their need for repentance, forgiveness, and Christ.
christFocus: Jesus sends the Spirit to convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment so sinners may be awakened to their need for the Savior.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Conviction is not the same as condemnation. Condemnation drives people into despair and hiding; conviction tells the truth so sinners may come into the light and find mercy in Christ.

The Holy Spirit exposes sin at the level of actions, desires, motives, unbelief, and self-rule. He does not wound for cruelty; He wounds in order to heal with truth and grace.

Conviction points to Jesus. The Spirit does not merely show people they are wrong; He shows them the Savior who is right, righteous, crucified, risen, and ready to forgive the repentant.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People in shame often confuse the Spirit's conviction with the enemy's accusation. This doctrine helps them recognize the difference: conviction leads toward Christ and repentance, while accusation tries to drive them away from hope.

It also protects against shallow comfort. People do not need to be affirmed in what destroys them; they need the Spirit's merciful truth leading them to freedom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When the Holy Spirit convicts you, do not hide or harden your heart. Confess sin honestly, run to Christ for mercy, receive correction as grace, and take the next step of repentance and obedience.
